title: Make tenant deletion archive-only, as the contract already requires
goal: DeleteTenant currently rejects a deletion only when the tenant has active members AND is not archived (tenant_service.go:596-604). A tenant left active with zero active memberships — reachable by deleting all of its users, which disables their memberships — can therefore be tombstoned directly, skipping the archive state that contract sections 2.1 and 2.2 require. This wave restores the contract rule: only an archived tenant may be deleted. The existing in-transaction membership disable stays, because an archived tenant may still carry active memberships and RemoveMember refuses to drop the last owner; that behaviour is what keeps the documented retirement path from deadlocking. The frontend stops offering delete on non-archived rows, and the contract, API doc and runbooks are aligned in the same wave.
findings: TC-02 (P2): tenant_service.go:596-604 guards with `memberCount > 0 && row.Status != tenant.TenantStatusArchived`, so an active tenant with zero active members is deletable. Contract sections 2.1 and 2.2 both state that deletion is allowed only for archived tenants.

Reachability: DeleteUser disables the user's memberships (user_membership.go:78-88), so deleting every user of a live tenant drives memberCount to zero without archiving it. The console delete action is enabled for every status, permission permitting (TenantList.tsx:511-522).
The current comment justifies allowing deletion of archived tenants with active members; this wave keeps that and removes only the non-archived bypass.

Fixture impact measured on 2026-10-27 with the suite green (119 tests): 14 DeleteTenant call sites in tests, and only tenant_lifecycle_guard_test.go:117-121 archives first. The other 13 delete a never-archived tenant and pass only because of the bypass — tenant_code_lifecycle_test.go (30, 61, 155, 221, 255, 273), tenant_lifecycle_guard_test.go (191, 216, 235), tenant_service_list_test.go (121, 187), tenant_service_test.go (456, 471). Enforcing the guard turns all of them red, so updating them is part of this wave, not an afterthought.

TestDeletedTenantRefusesNewMembers (tenant_lifecycle_guard_test.go:210-224) uses the bypass to build its tombstone fixture and then asserts AddMember returns ErrTenantNotFound. It must archive before deleting; the assertion itself stays valid.

in: Replace the DeleteTenant guard with `if row.Status != tenant.TenantStatusArchived { return ErrTenantNotArchived }`
Add ErrTenantNotArchived in tenant_service.go and map it in tenant_platform_handler.go failServiceError to a new i18n key tenant.not_archived
Keep the transaction body unchanged: disable active memberships, allocate the deleted code, write status=deleted
Register the new error and i18n key in docs/contracts/TENANT_CONTRACT_V1.md section 5, docs/api/TENANT_API.md and the frontend error mapping in the same wave
Disable the delete action in frontend/src/modules/system/iam/tenant/TenantList.tsx unless row.status === 'archived'; keep the Popconfirm for archived rows
Add a regression test in tenant_lifecycle_guard_test.go: an active tenant with zero active members is rejected with ErrTenantNotArchived
Update the 13 existing test fixtures that delete a never-archived tenant to archive first (the files and line numbers are listed in Findings); do not weaken the new guard to keep them green
Update docs/runbooks/TENANT_TROUBLESHOOTING.md and TENANT_MIGRATION_RUNBOOK.md wherever they describe deleting a non-archived tenant
out: Changing the status machine, the archived terminal state or the tombstone semantics
Changing RemoveMember, ensureNotLastOwner or the membership disable rules
Any migration or data repair for tenants already tombstoned without archiving
Making archive automatic on some other action
Changing routes or response envelopes beyond the new error code

implementationNotes: Search the test tree first: 13 existing call sites delete a non-archived tenant and encode the defect. Rewrite each to archive first, not delete the test and not relax the guard. Run the suite with PANTHEON_TEST_DSN set — without it 85 of the 119 tenant tests skip and the package reports ok in 0.04s, which hides exactly this breakage.
Error text must be a translation key, not prose; follow the existing tenant.* namespace used by failServiceError.
The UI disable is an affordance, not the enforcement; the backend guard must fail even when the request is issued directly.
Keep the two changes in separate commits (backend guard, frontend disable) so the backend fix can be bisected on its own.
If the maintainer prefers the looser rule, this wave closes as abandoned and the contract is amended instead; do not silently keep both.

executionRoles.implementerPosture: Write the failing test first, then change the guard; keep the transaction body untouched.
reviewerPosture: Confirm the new test fails against the old guard and passes against the new one.
Confirm archived tenants with active members are still deletable in one transaction.
Confirm the new error code appears in contract, API doc and frontend mapping.
Confirm the delete action is disabled for active, suspended and deleted rows.
